conviction_note: The print turns on the first formal FY2027 Adjusted EBITDA guide, from a CEO who took over on 1 October, against the company's own preliminary 'generally flat vs ~$1.48bn'. Since August the inflation and sector evidence has leaned against that number (feed costs, Conagra, Flowers) and egg prices are at 20-year lows. Against that, the stock already fell 12.8% when the flat FY27 was first floated, trades about 31% below its 52-week high at roughly 7.5x EV/EBITDA, and 12-15% of the float is short with 5.5 days to cover. My findings sum to -1.4 and the scaled number is -0.28. I size the move large (7.0, above the 6.32 median, because this is a first guide) and the sign close to a coin flip (p_up 48).

findings.finding: The print's main line is the first formal FY2027 Adjusted EBITDA guide. In its 2026-08-06 8-K the company gave only a preliminary 'generally flat' against a comparable base of about $1.48bn (FY26 $1,560-1,570M less about $60M of Foodservice above its $500M run rate and about $20M from divested businesses). On the call it added that inflation was tracking toward the high end, that retail pricing would lag costs into late FY27, and that the budget was still in development. So the risk is that the range is centred below $1.48bn, or that 'flat' comes with a wide range.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide line has driven every recent reaction. 2025-11-20 (initial FY26 guide $1.50-1.54bn): -7.15%. 2026-02-05 (FY26 raised to $1.55-1.58bn): +9.77%. 2026-08-06 (FY26 narrowed, FY27 'flat vs $1.48bn' floated): -12.79%.
findings.why_not_priced: Most of the 'flat' framing is already priced: the stock fell 12.8% on it and sits at about 7.5x EV/EBITDA. What is not priced is the gap between a preliminary 'flat' and a formal range. If the market expected a cut below $1.48bn, the stock would sit at the 52-week low ($71.45), not 11% above it after the October-November rebound to the mid-$80s.
findings.independence: Same Q3 document as the bar. The call commentary on inflation at the high end and pricing lagging is in https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/post-q3-earnings-call-highlights (2026-08-07). The preview at https://finviz.com/news/421343/post-holdings-faces-fy27-reckoning-as-egg-windfall-fades-and-deleveraging-takes-priority (2026-11-11) flags the same risk. Both restate the company.

findings.finding: This is the first guide and call under the new CEO. Nicolas Catoggio became President and CEO on 2026-10-01, and Rob Vitale moved to Executive Chairman. Vitale did not join the Q3 call. A first guide from a new CEO carries a higher chance of a conservative reset or a portfolio announcement than an incumbent's.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior CEO-transition print in the baseline. The guide line moved the stock -7.2%, +9.8% and -12.8% over the last three guide events.
findings.why_not_priced: The transition itself is public. What is unpriced is whether the first guide is set low to be beaten. If the market priced a reset, the FY27 'flat' anchor would already be absent from the preview, and it is not: the 2026-11-11 preview still anchors on flat vs $1.48bn.
findings.independence: https://www.fooddive.com/news/post-holdings-ceo-to-step-down/819657/ reports the same transition. The new-CEO reset point is my inference, not a document.

findings.finding: US egg markets collapsed through FY26 Q4. Jan-Aug 2026 Midwest wholesale large eggs averaged about $0.81/dozen and breaking stock (the input for further processing) about $0.16/dozen, a 20-year nominal low (WATTAgNet via UkrAgroConsult, 2026-09-29). Cal-Maine's Jun-Aug quarter showed conventional egg ASP down 59.3% YoY, and its guidance expects continued pricing pressure. For Post this backs the Foodservice normalization to the $500M run rate it already guided, and it raises the risk that Foodservice erodes faster. Late-October HPAI layer outbreaks (Illinois 934.6k birds, California about 1.3M) were under 0.5% of the flock.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Foodservice and egg normalization was the core of the 2026-08-06 -12.79% reaction (Foodservice segment profit -18.6% on lapping AI pricing).
findings.why_not_priced: Post's $500M run rate and its FY27 'growth from that base' were set in August, before Cal-Maine's 2026-09-30 print confirmed how far egg pricing fell. If the market believed Foodservice would undershoot $500M, previews would question the run rate rather than repeat it. Net of the rest of the company: Foodservice is about a third of EBITDA, and low breaking-stock cost partly offsets lower pass-through pricing, so this is sized small.
findings.independence: Cal-Maine Q1 FY27 release: https://finviz.com/news/396859/cal-maine-foods-reports-first-quarter-fiscal-2027-results (2026-09-30). A direct industry counterparty, but a shell-egg producer rather than a processor. The macro-to-Post transmission is a proxy.

findings.finding: Feed and grain inflation for 2027: layer feed costs are projected up about 8% in 2027, on corn about +16% and soybean meal about +5% (WATTAgNet via UkrAgroConsult, 2026-09-29). Peers that guided since mid-2026 cited persistent inflation. Conagra's FY27 guide came in weaker than expected on beef, oil-related inputs and logistics, with volumes down mid-single digits and the dividend halved. Flowers Foods cut its 2026 outlook a second time in November with volumes -7%. This is a proxy for Post's statement that inflation is at the high end and pricing lags into late FY27.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Inflation commentary was part of the -12.79% on 2026-08-06.
findings.source_date: 2026 (Conagra FY26 Q4 release, July 2026; exact date not confirmed from URL)
findings.why_not_priced: These are sector proxies. Post already said inflation is at the high end. What is open is whether FY27 cereal grain and pet ingredient costs land above the plan Post set in August. If the market had priced a further step-up, peers' moves would already show in POST's November tape, which instead rebounded.
findings.independence: Corn and feed projection: https://ukragroconsult.com/en/news/us-egg-producers-sell-below-cost-as-prices-hit-a-20-year-low/ (2026-09-29). Flowers cut: https://www.just-food.com/newsletters/flowers-foods-lowers-guidance-as-volume-pressures-persist (Nov 2026). Shares the egg finding's source for the feed number only.

findings.finding: Peer cereal read-through: General Mills' Sep 2026 quarter (FQ1 FY27, reported 2026-09-23, after Post last spoke) showed its cereal share decline narrowing to 0.1 points from 0.9 a year earlier, with NAR organic sales -3% (volume -2%, price/mix -1%) and the full-year outlook reaffirmed. This fits Post's expectation that cereal volumes move toward the long-run -1 to -2% category trend in FY27.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Post Consumer Brands improvement (segment adj EBITDA +11.2% in Q3, helped by 8th Avenue) was overshadowed by Foodservice on 2026-08-06.
findings.why_not_priced: General Mills is the largest cereal peer and spoke after Post. Previews still describe Post's cereal as 'improving slowly'. A share gain for General Mills is ambiguous for Post's own volume, so it is sized small.

findings.finding: Pet food read-through: Smucker's quarter to 2026-07-31 (reported 2026-08-26) showed US Retail Pet Foods sales +1% and segment profit -2%. Meow Mix was +4% with dry-cat volume growth, while Post said its competing Nine Lives brand showed more price sensitivity than expected and its Nutrish relaunch missed its flat-to-growth goal.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Pet volumes fell 14% in Q2 FY26 (2026-05-07 print: -0.91%), so a pet weakness print has moved the stock little.
findings.why_not_priced: A competitor's dry-cat volume growth while Nine Lives was price-sensitive suggests share loss in Post's quarter. The market treats pet as a known drag, so this is small.
findings.independence: Post's own Nine Lives and Nutrish comments are in the Earnings Whispers preview: https://finviz.com/news/421343/post-holdings-faces-fy27-reckoning-as-egg-windfall-fades-and-deleveraging-takes-priority (2026-11-11).

findings.finding: Q4 is pinned by the guide. FY26 Adjusted EBITDA guidance of $1,560-1,570M less 9M adjusted EBITDA of $1,190.5M ($813.2M six-month per the Q2 8-K plus $377.3M Q3) implies Q4 adj EBITDA of $369.5-379.5M, against $377.3M in Q3. Single-source consensus is EPS $1.66 and revenue about $1.98bn. In Q3 Post beat EPS by about 3.5% and missed revenue by about 4.4%, partly because Crystal Farms was sold on 2026-05-01.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2026: EPS beat with a revenue miss, -12.79% (driven by the guide). Q2 2026: affirmed, -0.91%.
findings.why_not_priced: Inside the company's guided range, so the market was told to expect it. Sized near zero. A modest beat is the base case, given the company's pattern of narrowing around the midpoint.
findings.independence: The Q3 figures come from https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001530950/000153095026000076/ex99-1q32026er.htm (2026-08-06), the same company documents.

findings.finding: Capital allocation is shifting from buybacks to debt paydown. Post bought 9.1M shares for $908.8M (average $100.34) in the 9M, plus 0.4M for $39.3M at $88.80 through 2026-08-05, and has $490.7M of authorization left. Net leverage is 4.6x, Q3 net interest is $108.2M against $88.5M a year earlier, and FY26 capex is $370-390M. The FY27 framework will say how much of free cash flow goes to debt and how much to buybacks at about $79.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: A new $500M authorization accompanied the FY25 Q4 print (2025-11-20, -7.15%, driven by the guide).
findings.why_not_priced: The pivot to deleveraging is in the preview, so it is priced. The open question is whether the new CEO resumes buybacks at a price about 21% below the FY26 average purchase price. It could go either way, hence zero.

findings.finding: Positioning: about 5.6M shares short with 5.5 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 settlement, roughly 12-15% of float after the share count fell about 17% from buybacks. The stock is 30.9% below its 52-week high and 9.2% above its low, at about 7.5x EV/EBITDA ($79.23 x about 47M shares plus $7.41bn net debt, over $1.48bn). A guide that merely confirms 'flat' could trigger short covering.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-02-05: a modest raise on a depressed stock produced +9.77%. Each of the three guide events since 2025-11 moved the stock at least 7%.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest that is not covered into the print is a mechanism of its own. If shorts had covered, the November settlement would be down sharply, and Benzinga reports only 'declining'. The data is snippet-only and six weeks old, so it is sized modestly.

baseline_tension: There is no usable skew. My lean is mildly negative on the guide, which agrees with the -3.4% 20-day drift and the 31% drawdown. It cuts against a 12-15%-of-float short and a valuation that already priced the August 'flat FY27' reset, so p_up sits near 50.
